From: Leah Park <procurement@asteriumhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and residency question (EU + APAC pilot)

Hi Jonas,

Hope you're well. Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal in August and procurement asked I get ahead of the regional controls and capacity we discussed earlier. A few constraints from our side:
- Primary data residency for EU traffic must be in a EU-only tenant (GDPR requirements).
- We want to run an APAC pilot during Q4 (staged onramp) with a small burst pool and a cross-region failover pathway.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~120M/month at launch, with a 6 month ramp to 300M/month.

Can you confirm whether a 12-month renewal can include a staged APAC onramp and a residency carve-out for EU, or whether you require a 24-month committed term to enable the discounts and reserved capacity? Also please send a draft SOW and indicative pricing so we can start legal review.

I'm copying Amin (tech) for any clarifying technical questions.

Thanks,
Leah
Leah Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Asterium Health
procurement@asteriumhealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and residency question (EU + APAC pilot)

Hi Leah — thanks for the clear constraints. Short answers up front: yes, we can support an EU-only residency carve-out and a staggered APAC onramp; the economics change depending on committed term and reserved throughput.

Proposal summary (high level):
- Term options: 12 months (no long-term commitment discounts) or 24 months (preferred) with a 15-25% committed capacity discount depending on GPU tier.
- APAC pilot: staged onramp over 3 months, with a dedicated standby pool for failover. We recommend an initially small reserved APAC pool (10% of peak) with burst access to cloud providers.
- Data residency: EU traffic pinned to EU tenancy nodes; logs and telemetry can be routed to EU KMS on request (we'll need a short SOC/controls confirmation).

I've attached a draft SOW and a preliminary pricing matrix for your team to review (Asterium_SOW_v3.pdf, pricing_matrix_apac_onsite.csv). Can we book 30 minutes on Thursday to walk through the ramp and failover model with your tech leads?

Next steps:
1) Review attached SOW/pricing and confirm preferred term (12 vs 24).
2) Ops (neha) will validate the residency gating and failover constraints with your team.
3) If economics are agreed, we will produce a final SOW and DocuSign envelope.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

— Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachment(s): Asterium_SOW_v3.pdf; pricing_matrix_apac_onsite.csv

Subject: Re: Renewal and residency question (EU + APAC pilot) — ops notes

Amin / Jonas — technical notes for the ops/architecture review:

EU data residency and segmentation:
- EU production traffic will be served from our eu-west tenancy (pinning at the customer tenancy layer). Backups and audit logs can be configured to remain in the eu KMS boundary.
- We will provide a data_residency_matrix.xlsx that maps data classes (PII, telemetry, logs) to storage and transit policies. See attached.

APAC onramp + failover:
- Staged onramp: Month 0–3: warm standby with prefix caching; Month 3–6: ramp reserved capacity; Month 6+: full production.
- Cross-region failover: automatic routing to APAC standby nodes on eu node failure. RTO target: 60s under warm KV conditions, but note cold-cache failover can increase latency for the first 10K tokens per session.
- Required approvals: cross-border telemetry replication and emergency log access for our support squad. We'll provide a runbook for the cutover.

I'll coordinate a short ops session with your tech and security leads — proposed times next Tue/Wed.

Neha Kapoor
Director, Regional Ops (EU)
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachment(s): data_residency_matrix.xlsx
